name: LMNA cardiomyopathy
aliases: LMNA dilated cardiomyopathy with conduction disease

reference.source: Standard cardiology and inherited cardiac conditions references
clinicalPearls: Caused by variants in LMNA, encoding the nuclear envelope proteins lamin A and C, and characterised by dilated cardiomyopathy with prominent conduction system disease
The typical sequence is early atrioventricular conduction disturbance and atrial arrhythmia, followed by ventricular arrhythmia and progressive left ventricular dysfunction
It carries a notably high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmia and sudden death, which can precede or exceed the degree of pump failure
Because sudden death may occur even with only mildly reduced ejection fraction, defibrillator implantation is considered at a lower threshold than in many other cardiomyopathies
Skeletal muscle involvement (Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy or limb-girdle patterns) may coexist, reflecting the wider laminopathy spectrum
Recognised high-risk markers include non-sustained ventricular tachycardia, male sex, non-missense variants, and progressive reduction in ejection fraction
Family screening is essential given autosomal dominant inheritance and the arrhythmic risk in relatives
reference.pathophysiology: Lamins A and C form a meshwork underlying the inner nuclear membrane that provides structural support to the nucleus and regulates gene expression and mechanotransduction. Pathogenic LMNA variants weaken this nuclear lamina, rendering cardiomyocytes and their conduction-system counterparts vulnerable to mechanical stress and abnormal signalling. This leads to progressive fibrosis and cell loss, first affecting the atria and the specialised conduction tissue, causing conduction block and atrial arrhythmia, and later the ventricular myocardium, producing chamber dilatation, systolic dysfunction and a substrate for re-entrant ventricular arrhythmia. The disproportionate arrhythmic and conduction burden relative to the degree of ventricular impairment is the defining clinical hallmark.
additionalDifferentials: Idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy of other genetic cause (for example titin)
Other muscular dystrophies with cardiac involvement
additionalInvestigations: Serial 12-lead ECGs to detect evolving conduction disease and atrial arrhythmia
Ambulatory ECG monitoring for non-sustained ventricular tachycardia
Echocardiography to assess chamber size and systolic function
Cardiac MRI to quantify function and detect myocardial fibrosis
Genetic testing of LMNA with cascade family screening
Creatine kinase and neurological assessment where skeletal myopathy is suspected
redFlags: High-grade atrioventricular block or need for pacing at a young age
Progressive fall in left ventricular ejection fraction
Family history of sudden death or LMNA-confirmed disease
reference.prognosis: LMNA cardiomyopathy is among the more aggressive inherited cardiomyopathies, with high rates of malignant arrhythmia, progressive heart failure and sudden death; outcome is improved by early rhythm surveillance, defibrillator therapy in high-risk patients, and heart failure management, with transplantation for end-stage disease.
pitfalls: Applying standard ejection-fraction-based defibrillator thresholds and underestimating arrhythmic risk
Attributing early conduction disease to benign causes and missing the underlying laminopathy
Failing to screen relatives who may harbour the variant and face sudden-death risk
references: ESC guidelines on cardiomyopathies and on prevention of sudden cardiac death
